method: Treated A1's review as a new artifact to falsify, not as corroboration merely because its conclusions agree with B's independent review.
Checked the review against the user's required review-object shape: resolves map keyed by finding ID, sealedPropertiesCovered back-references, knownLimitations, and confidence.
Followed every status/authority claim changed by the convergence through architecture/06, architecture/09, architecture/11, and the authoritative register.
Compared artifact lifecycle status separately from claim status so CANDIDATE review state could not silently replace REOPENED claim state.
Asked whether the traceability document's graduation language constrains the greenfield design or leaks hypothetical decisions into product records.
whatCouldHaveFailed: The second review could agree substantively while failing the machine-checkable review contract.
A partial D9 authority repair could leave another document elevating the demoted detailed contract.
Retention v4 could be reviewed in one place and still called unreviewed or merely CANDIDATE elsewhere.
The traceability document could simultaneously forbid and require graduation out of the local tree.
The canonical checker could remain green because these semantic conflicts are outside its syntactic coverage.
positiveAssessment: A1 independently reconstructed the D9 invariant inventory and R-1 boundary before diffing the extraction; this is meaningfully different from B's authority/dependency crosswalk.
The two reviews converge on the missing D9 semantic partition, erased R-1 boundary, invalid percentage instrument, form-based altitude rule, finding laundering, and absent design handoff.
A1 correctly retained the scope correction's direction while rejecting it as binding.

findings.title: A1's substantive review lacks the required resolves map and places a candidate rule under sealedPropertiesCovered
evidence: scope-correction-a3.v1.review-a1.json defines A1-SC-01..08 but has no resolves member
the exercise explicitly requires every review JSON to carry a resolves map keyed to finding IDs
sealedPropertiesCovered includes 'architecture vs detailed design altitude (candidate rule)' even though METHOD.ALTITUDE remains CANDIDATE and unbound
findings.impact: The review is persuasive human evidence but is not itself a compliant closure object. Treating it as ratification would repeat the prose-agreement failure the artifact rule was introduced to prevent.
findings.requiredChange: Agent 1 should author an amendment adding A1-SC-01..08 dispositions and move the candidate altitude item out of sealedPropertiesCovered into an explicitly candidate-properties field. B must not silently rewrite another reviewer's attestation.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A documented exception to the user's mandatory review schema or an A1-authored amendment satisfying it.

findings.title: Traceability still elevated demoted D9 and R-1 detailed contracts after the register made both unbound
evidence: architecture/11 listed d9-exit-contract.v1.5 and r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.3 as Candidate artifacts
the same section said checkable artifacts are the binding form of any CANDIDATE decision
the register has bindingArtifact null for D9 and R-1 and records both scope-correction extractions as rejected candidates
check-claims remained clean because its version check cannot relate differently named authority objects
findings.impact: A reader following the traceability inventory would still treat detailed exploration as architecture authority despite both independent reviews rejecting that rebind.
findings.requiredChange: Mark v1.5/v1.3 non-binding, add the rejected scope extraction, and say the register—not the inventory—owns current status. Presentation repair applied in this turn.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A documented layer in which architecture/11's Candidate label referred only to artifact lifecycle and explicitly denied architecture authority; it did neither.

findings.title: Retention v4 was simultaneously reviewed, unreviewed, CANDIDATE, and REOPENED across four authority surfaces
evidence: retention-tiers.v4.review-a1.json completed an independent review with required changes
architecture/06 heading said 'not sealed or independently reviewed'
architecture/09 called the claim CANDIDATE and the design unreviewed while the register called ARCH.RETENTION-TIERS REOPENED and said A1 accepted v4
the register's v4 disposition still said CANDIDATE-UNREVIEWED and TM blockers called v4 unreviewed
findings.impact: Artifact lifecycle and claim status were conflated. A reader could miss both the historical reopening and the specific A1 required changes while the checker reported clean.
findings.requiredChange: Keep the claim REOPENED; label v4 CANDIDATE-REVIEWED-REQUIRED-CHANGES; update 06/09/register/TM wording; register the 09 restatement. Presentation repair applied in this turn.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that A1's filed review had been withdrawn or did not review v4; neither is true.

findings.title: Traceability both forbade and required sealed decisions to leave the local tree
evidence: architecture/11 graduation table says sealed decisions stay here and must not enter the shipping product's ADR log
the final blockquote says 'Everything sealed should leave here'
the register scopeNote says the tree is a hypothetical greenfield design and earlier graduation instructions are withdrawn
findings.impact: The last sentence can reintroduce the exact migration/product-record contamination the coordinator removed, or authorize an unspecified external write.
findings.requiredChange: State that impermanence is an accepted risk and that any future durable home requires an explicit coordinator decision; do not infer product-ADR graduation. Presentation repair applied in this turn.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: An explicit coordinator-approved durable destination outside this local exercise; none is recorded.

findings.title: Architecture/09's statement that every open-decision row is unreviewed is false
evidence: the register links completed reviews for threat, operability, versioning, resolved inputs, delivery, fact identity, and retention
architecture/09 nevertheless says every row is authored but unreviewed
reviewed-with-blockers is materially different from unreviewed
findings.impact: The blanket wording erases review evidence and the distinction between unknown defects and known unresolved blockers.
findings.requiredChange: Replace it with a mixed-review-state warning and direct readers to the register. Presentation repair applied in this turn.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: If 'unreviewed' were explicitly defined to mean 'not sealed'; it is not, and the method treats those states separately.

resolves.B-SCC-01: OPEN-BLOCKER: A1 must supply its own compliant amendment; B did not alter A1's attestation.
resolves.B-SCC-02: PRESENTATION-FIX-APPLIED: architecture/11 now classifies D9 v1.5 and R-1 v1.3 as non-binding and the scope extraction as rejected.
resolves.B-SCC-03: PRESENTATION-FIX-APPLIED: claim status remains REOPENED while v4 lifecycle is REVIEWED-REQUIRED-CHANGES across artifact, prose, and register.
resolves.B-SCC-04: PRESENTATION-FIX-APPLIED: contradictory graduation instruction removed; no external/product write authorised.
resolves.B-SCC-05: PRESENTATION-FIX-APPLIED: architecture/09 now states review status is mixed and register-owned.

sealedPropertiesCovered: architecture/10 method rule 4 — artifacts back-reference the decisions they encode
architecture/10 method rule 7 — unreviewed claims are not settled premises
architecture/10 method rule 8 — status attaches to claims rather than containers
register scopeNote — the hypothetical greenfield tree does not graduate into shipping-product ADRs
knownLimitations: This audit does not author scope-correction v2, D9 architecture v2, or R-1 architecture v2.
It does not independently repeat A1's full D9/R-1 semantic diff; B's prior independent review already records that work.
The repairs make current authority honest but do not extend check-claims to detect semantic aliases, exact REOPENED-vs-CANDIDATE drift, or contradictory prose.
B cannot make A1's review artifact compliant without corrupting reviewer authorship; B-SCC-01 remains open.
confidence: high on artifact-shape and cross-document contradictions; medium-high that all remaining authority aliases have been found because the checker does not enumerate semantic restatements
sealRecommendation: The two independent reviews justify rejecting scope-correction v1, not sealing a replacement. Do not count A1's review as a compliant closure artifact until A1 supplies its resolves amendment.
